Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second chapter to unfold! The Irish players are taking their fielding positions. Dilara Akter and Juairiya Ferdous will open the innings for Bangladesh Women. It will be spin to start for Ireland as Aimee Maguire has the new ball in hand. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The stage is set - So, 144 is the target on the board and by all means, Bangladesh have enough firepower in their batting unit to chase it down. However, if Ireland chip in some early wickets inside the Powerplay, just like their opposition did, things might get even more exciting. Stay tuned as the second inning will start anytime soon.

From steady ship to total collapse - With the fall of the third wicket, Orla Prendergast couldn't help much as she was eliminated by Sharmin Akhter. Leah Paul and Rebecca Stokell steadied the ship, rotating the strike intelligently to keep the scoreboard ticking while never shying away from punishing the bad delivery when it arrived. Their partnership blossomed into a composed 43-run stand that gave Ireland's innings renewed purpose. But the moment Paul fell, the floodgates opened once again. The wickets tumbled yet again, and no batter was able to offer crucial runs on the board. Later on, it was the tail enders, Christina Coulter Reilly and Ava Canning, who took matters into their hand and stepped up to get their score across the 140 mark. Bangladesh's bowlers swarmed in for the kill. Shajida Akhter ended up picking 3 wickets, Marufa Akter claimed two, while Ritu Moni, Nahida Akter, Sobhana Mostary and Rubeya Khatun each chipped in with one to complete a clinical, collective dismantling of the Irish lower order.

Bangladesh starts with flying colours - Bangladesh Women made an excellent start with the ball, with Marufa Akter and Sanjida Akter Meghla picking up two crucial wickets inside the Powerplay to put Ireland firmly under pressure. However, the final over brought a decisive shift in momentum, Orla Prendergast and Gaby Lewis unleashed their attacking instincts, plundering 16 runs to ease the pressure. Ireland closed the Powerplay at 42 for 2, but the reprieve was short-lived. Marufa returned almost immediately to remove the dangerous looking Gaby Lewis.

Bangladesh gets the upper hand - Bangladesh's bowlers were all over Ireland throughout the inning, but skipper Nigar Sultana would feel that his bowlers had leaked a few extra runs here and there. 31 runs were scored in the last two overs, and the credit goes to Christina Coulter Reilly and Ava Canning as they batted brilliantly to post 143 runs on the board.

What a finish and Ava Canning has single-handedly given Ireland Women a fighting chance as they finish with 143/9 on the board. Floated up outside off, Ava Canning goes after it and slices it away down the ground, towards long off and the batters manage to come back for the second run.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Bangladesh Women. It will be the duo of Amy Hunter and Alana Dalzell to open the innings for Ireland Women. Marufa Akter has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Cameron Steel is pitchside with his valuable insights. He starts off saying that the weather is looking great today, and the match will take place on a used pitch. Adds that it's firm, but the spinners might get some turn on it. The batters will enjoy playing on it, and they will target the shorter side of the boundary. Ends up saying that the outfield is looking quick today, and he feels that it's going to be a wonderful day of cricket.

The captain of Ireland Women - Gaby Lewis says that they wanted to bat first anyway, and it looks like a good wicket. Adds that Bangladesh are a team that they know well and are looking forward to preparing well for the main event. On Orla Prendergast, she says that she was just rested and is ready to go again, and finishes by saying that they will look to rotate all their 15 players.

The captain of Bangladesh Women - Nigar Sultana starts off saying that she wants to see how their bowlers bowl on this condition, as for that reason, they have opted to bowl first. Adds that the start hasn't been good for them in these warm-up fixtures, but she feels like they are getting used to the conditions. About their preparation for the match, she says that it's a wonderful opportunity for them to prepare before the big stages.

Bangladesh Women - Dilara Akter (WK), Juairiya Ferdous, Sharmin Akhter, Nigar Sultana (C), Sobhana Mostary, Shorna Akter, Ritu Moni, Taj Nehar, Fahima Khatun, Nahida Akter, Marufa Akter, Rabeya Khan, Sultana Khatun, Sanjida Akter Meghla, and Fariha Trisna.

Ireland Women - Amy Hunter (WK), Alana Dalzell, Gaby Lewis (C), Orla Prendergast, Rebecca Stokell, Leah Paul, Louise Little, Alice Tector, Christina Coulter Reilly, Arlene Kelly, Ava Canning, Lara McBride, Cara Murray, Georgina Dempsey, Aimee Maguire, and Laura Delany.
TOSS - The coin flip lands in favour of Bangladesh Women. They will BOWL first.

Ireland seeking vengeance - What makes this fixture genuinely compelling, beyond the pre-tournament context, is the underlying rivalry between these two sides that has quietly been building. The last time these teams met in a World Cup-related setting, Bangladesh defeated Ireland by seven runs in a qualifier, which certainly left a scar on Irish memories. Therefore, the stakes, even in a warm-up, feel very real. Stay tuned for toss and further updates...

Tale of Two Forms - For Ireland, the energy around this squad is palpable. For Ireland, the energy around this squad is palpable. They arrived at the tournament on the back of a tri-series campaign against Pakistan and West Indies in late May and early June 2026, finishing second in the standings, a solid run of competitive cricket that has given them real match rhythm heading into the group stage. Much of that momentum runs through one name, Orla Prendergast. At just 23, Prendergast already carries the weight of a match-winner who has seen both extremes of the international game. Bangladesh, meanwhile, have entered the tournament with not strong T20I form, having been swept 3-0 by Sri Lanka in their most recent bilateral assignment.

Greetings folks - There is something deeply fitting about these two teams sharing a warm-up fixture. Ireland and Bangladesh are perhaps the two sides in this tournament whose journeys to England have been the most hard-fought, the most emotionally charged, and the most richly deserved. Both teams earned their place at the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 through the global qualifier, battling through pressure-cooker knockout cricket just to stand where they stand today. This warm-up is not just preparation, it is a celebration of everything both nations have sacrificed to get here. Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to one of the most spirited contests this warm-up window has to offer.

A crucial rehearsal in Loughborough - The Ireland Women head into this World Cup warm-up fixture with a clinical, fearless blueprint that has completely transformed their visual identity on the world stage. No longer just a team trying to compete, they are a unit that commands respect, moving through a journey that saw them push boundaries in the Global Qualifier earlier this year. Standing across from them are the Bangladesh Women, the battle-hardened tigresses who know exactly how to manage tournament pressure. Neither team had a good start to these warm-up fixtures. Bangladesh they have faced the defending champions, the Kiwis, before this encounter, where they faced a loss by 68 runs after conceding 193. On the other side, the story is pretty similar, Ireland have faced the runner-up of the 2024 edition, South Africa, where they lost by just 15 runs.
